Only this one test is the sole `*AgentTest` file and confirms the same single failure.

## Summary

Created `gson/src/test/java/com/google/gson/stream/JsonReaderAgentTest.java` (self-contained, JUnit 3.8 style, matching the project's existing tests) with 47 tests covering happy paths plus boundary/error cases: empty/nested structures, strict vs. lenient parsing, number edge cases (`Long.MIN_VALUE`, leading zeros, int/long precision loss), string escapes, malformed unicode escapes, `skipValue`, `getPath`, non-execute prefix, comments, unquoted/single-quoted tokens, closed-reader behavior, and EOF handling.

**46 tests pass. 1 test fails, revealing a real bug:**

- `testTopLevelValueWithoutLenientThrows` — `JsonReader`'s own Javadoc for `setLenient` states that in strict (non-lenient) mode, lenient parsing is required for "Top-level values of any type. With strict parsing, the top-level value must be an object or an array." However, `doPeek()`'s handling of `JsonScope.EMPTY_DOCUMENT` never actually enforces this: it only conditionally consumes the non-execute prefix when lenient, then unconditionally falls through to the general value-parsing switch, which accepts booleans/numbers/strings without ever calling `checkLenient()`. As a result, `new JsonReader(new StringReader("true")).nextBoolean()` succeeds and returns `true` even with lenient left at its default `false`, contradicting the documented contract (and inconsistent with `JsonWriter`, which does enforce this symmetric restriction, per `JsonWriterTest.testInvalidTopLevelTypes`).

I used a temporary `_scratch` directory outside the test tree to manually confirm this and one other borderline behavior while writing tests; it has been deleted, and no files other than `JsonReaderAgentTest.java` were created or modified.
